items.stem: Who can create a Glean support ticket directly?

options.text: Any user with a Gleaniverse account.
Designated Support Contacts, as defined in the Glean Support Agreement.

items.stem: A user who is not a Designated Support Contact finds a bug they can reproduce. What is the documented next step?

options.text: Post the full error log in the community forum.
Wait for the next monthly product update.
Start a conversation, or ask their Glean administrator to submit a ticket.

items.stem: Which ticket detail lets support correlate the issue with system logs?

options.text: The date and time the issue occurred, with the timezone.
The name of the customer's executive sponsor.
A note asking support to raise the priority.

items.stem: The Service is unavailable to a subset of users. Which priority does the SLA example match?

options.text: Urgent priority, because any outage is critical.
Low priority, because most users can still work.
High priority, because only some users lose the Service.

items.stem: Which incidents are eligible for SLA response times?

options.text: Any incident raised by email, chat, or phone.
Only incidents submitted through the Glean support portal.
Only incidents raised by the partner.

items.stem: A Designated Support Contact cannot see the Tickets section in the support widget. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: They have not created a ticket yet. The section appears after the first ticket.
They must go directly to ticket.glean.com.
Tickets are only visible to Glean employees.
